pen noun

also ballpoint, ballpoint pen

classical

Quint. 10.3.31: quoad intinguntur calamī (Lewis & Short)
Hor. AP 447
Andresian p. 12
Traupman 30: calamus scrīptōrius
Traupman 27

calamus, calamī m.

noun, second declension

a pen that writes in ink

The Roman pen, a reed dipped in ink (ātrāmentum), and the natural word for a pen today; the Polis Institute’s course uses it so. The stilus scratched wax.

Other words

  • stilus, stilī m.

    noun, second declension · also used · modern

    Classically the pointed stylus for wax tablets; also said of a modern pen.

  • stilus sphaerātus — ballpoint

    also used · modern · Traupman 28

  • penna, pennae f. — a quill pen

    noun, first declension · also used · late Latin · Isid. Orig. 6.14 (Lewis & Short): calamus et penna: sed calamus arboris est, penna avis; Traupman 30

    Classically a feather or wing; “pen” only in late Latin.

See also notepad.
